cases.sentence: Я от Грицки (так они звали ___), тебя ждут.
cases.explain: «полкового командира» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “You’re always just as if you’d come out of a bath after it,” said Petritsky. “I’ve come from Gritsky’s” (that was what they called the colonel); “they’re expecting you.”

cases.sentence: – Да, это у него музыка? – сказал он, прислушиваясь к долетавшим до него ___ трубных басов, полек и вальсов. – Что за праздник?
cases.explain: «знакомым звукам» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Yes; is that music at his place?” he said, listening to the familiar sounds of polkas and waltzes floating across to him. “What’s the fête?”

cases.sentence: Серпуховской был ___, и он был рад ему.
cases.explain: «добрый приятель» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Having once made up his mind that he was happy in his love, that he sacrificed his ambition to it—having anyway taken up this position, Vronsky was incapable of feeling either envious of Serpuhovskoy or hurt with him for not coming first to him when he came to the regiment. Serpuhovskoy was a good friend, and he was delighted he had come.

cases.sentence: ___ Демин занимал большой помещичий дом.
cases.explain: «Полковой командир» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The colonel, Demin, had taken a large country house. The whole party were in the wide lower balcony. In the courtyard the first objects that met Vronsky’s eyes were a band of singers in white linen coats, standing near a barrel of vodka, and the robust, good-humored figure of the colonel surrounded by officers. He had gone out as far as the first step of the balcony and was loudly shouting across the band that played Offenbach’s quadrille, waving his arms and giving some orders to a few soldiers standing on one side. A group of soldiers, a quartermaster, and several subalterns came up to the balcony with Vronsky. The colonel returned to the table, went out again onto the steps with a tumbler in his hand, and proposed the toast, “To the health of our former comrade, the gallant general, Prince Serpuhovskoy. Hurrah!”

cases.sentence: – Ну, вот и он! – вскрикнул ___. – А мне сказал Яшвин, что ты в своем мрачном духе.
cases.explain: «полковой командир» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Here he is!” shouted the colonel. “Yashvin told me you were in one of your gloomy tempers.”

cases.sentence: – Займитесь им! – крикнул Яшвину ___, указывая на Вронского, и сошел вниз к солдатам.
cases.explain: «полковой командир» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “You look after him,” the colonel shouted to Yashvin, pointing to Vronsky; and he went down below to the soldiers.

cases.sentence: Кутеж у ___ продолжался долго.
cases.explain: «полкового командира» — after the preposition «у», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The fête at the colonel’s lasted a long while. There was a great deal of drinking. They tossed Serpuhovskoy in the air and caught him again several times. Then they did the same to the colonel. Then, to the accompaniment of the band, the colonel himself danced with Petritsky. Then the colonel, who began to show signs of feebleness, sat down on a bench in the courtyard and began demonstrating to Yashvin the superiority of Russia over Prussia, especially in cavalry attack, and there was a lull in the revelry for a moment. Serpuhovskoy went into the house to the bathroom to wash his hands and found Vronsky there; Vronsky was drenching his head with water. He had taken off his coat and put his sunburnt, hairy neck under the tap, and was rubbing it and his head with his hands. When he had finished, Vronsky sat down by Serpuhovskoy. They both sat down in the bathroom on a lounge, and a conversation began which was very interesting to both of them.

cases.sentence: – Она дружна с Варей, и это ___ петербургские, с которыми мне приятно видеться, – улыбаясь, ответил Вронский.
cases.explain: «единственные женщины» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “She’s friendly with Varya, and they’re the only women in Petersburg I care about seeing,” answered Vronsky, smiling. He smiled because he foresaw the topic the conversation would turn on, and he was glad of it.

cases.sentence: – Да и я о тебе знал, но не только чрез твою жену, – ___ лица запрещая этот намек, сказал Вронский. – Я очень рад был твоему успеху, и нисколько не удивлен.
cases.explain: «строгим выражением» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Yes; and I heard news of you, but not only through your wife,” said Vronsky, checking his hint by a stern expression of face. “I was greatly delighted to hear of your success, but not a bit surprised. I expected even more.”

cases.sentence: И я думаю, что ___ хорош, но ты его сделал не так, как надо.
cases.explain: «самый поступок» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “There it’s out! here it comes!” said Serpuhovskoy, laughing. “Ever since I heard about you, about your refusal, I began. … Of course, I approved of what you did. But there are ways of doing everything. And I think your action was good in itself, but you didn’t do it quite in the way you ought to have done.”

cases.sentence: Это ___, так же как этот наш хозяин.

cases.translation: “Very well off—for the time. But you’re not satisfied with that. I wouldn’t say this to your brother. He’s a nice child, like our host here. There he goes!” he added, listening to the roar of “hurrah!”—“and he’s happy, but that does not satisfy you.”

cases.translation: “But why so?” Vronsky mentioned a few men who were in power. “Why aren’t they independent men?”

cases.translation: “We’re coming directly!” Vronsky shouted to an officer, who looked into the room and called them to the colonel.

cases.sentence: Женщины – это ___ преткновения в деятельности человека.
cases.explain: «главный камень» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “And here’s my opinion for you. Women are the chief stumbling block in a man’s career. It’s hard to love a woman and do anything. There’s only one way of having love conveniently without its being a hindrance—that’s marriage. How, how am I to tell you what I mean?” said Serpuhovskoy, who liked similes. “Wait a minute, wait a minute! Yes, just as you can only carry a fardeau and do something with your hands, when the fardeau is tied on your back, and that’s marriage. And that’s what I felt when I was married. My hands were suddenly set free. But to drag that fardeau about with you without marriage, your hands will always be so full that you can do nothing. Look at Mazankov, at Krupov. They’ve ruined their careers for the sake of women.”
